source.title: Play a prepared Study escape attempt with all three investigators

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Approved bounded work meeting execution-readiness requirements

source.body:
## Problem Statement

Joel can play the accepted Jacqueline/Patrice skill-test experiment and Tony's prepared turn, but cannot yet coordinate turns across the three investigators and see their combined decisions change the scenario. The next bottleneck is connected party play through the actual rules, tabletop, save/resume and replay paths, while the program handles administration and Joel retains the decisions.

## Solution

Offer a **prepared Study escape attempt** in original The Gathering on Standard. Joel chooses investigator order, investigates, supports tests with other investigators, uses Jacqueline's reaction and weighs Patrice's Lucky! options. At the first fully settled action that gives the party six clues, he chooses whether to spend them and advance Act 1, including its actual map transition. If all investigator turns end first, the attempt finishes without escaping.

The endpoint is visible before play. This is a bounded task from a prepared position, not original scenario setup, a complete investigation phase on every branch, or a complete scenario. It does not force success. Ending the experiment preserves unfinished turns and does not invent defeat, victory or campaign consequences.

Joel accepted the direction, concrete position, endpoint, testing seam and prospective allowance on 2026-10-31, then explicitly invoked `to-spec` to publish this issue. The allowance is **32 aggregate active engineering hours**, including delegated work, source preflight, implementation, asset preparation, verification and review, plus **two owner sessions of at most 20 minutes each**, including retries. No paid services. The ceiling is not a calibrated delivery estimate.

## User Stories

1. As Joel, I want the prepared position and endpoint explained before play, so that I understand the task's limits.
2. As Joel, I want to choose which eligible investigator acts next, so that I can coordinate the party's approach.
3. As Joel, I want each investigator's turn and action allowance tracked separately, so that I do not administer turn order manually.
4. As Joel, I want camera focus to remain independent of the acting investigator, so that looking around cannot change who acts.
5. As Joel, I want each investigator's hand, resources, clues and condition visible, so that I can assess my options.
6. As Joel, I want to Investigate, Draw or gain a Resource with legal costs and consequences, so that I can make genuine tradeoffs.
7. As Joel, I want to end a turn early, so that the program does not force me to spend every action.
8. As Joel, I want unavailable actions refused for their actual rules reason, so that unsupported behavior is not disguised as a legal option.
9. As Joel, I want to choose my own matching commitments, so that I control the resources spent on a test.
10. As Joel, I want other investigators at the location to support a test within their legal limits, so that cooperation matters.
11. As Joel, I want Promise of Power's icons and curse cost administered together, so that its benefit and consequence remain connected.
12. As Joel, I want to choose when Jacqueline intervenes, including an eligible later curse reveal, so that her limited reaction remains my decision.
13. As Joel, I want all legal cancellation choices, including poor choices, so that the program does not choose strategy for me.
14. As Joel, I want random draws to respect physical token multiplicities and held tokens, so that the bag behaves correctly.
15. As Joel, I want each testing investigator's own elder-sign effect, so that Jacqueline helping someone does not replace their identity.
16. As Joel, I want the actual cost and fast timing of Lucky!, so that spending actions to draw it and gain resources is a meaningful alternative.
17. As Joel, I want any reachable Patrice elder-sign choice, including choosing the retained discard, so that optional effects are not silently skipped.
18. As Joel, I want arithmetic, modifiers, costs and outcomes explained in history, so that I can understand the rules without administering them.
19. As Joel, I want to choose whether to spend the six clues, so that the program does not force act advancement.
20. As Joel, I want advancement to move the party and change the map according to the real act, so that cooperation has a visible scenario consequence.
21. As Joel, I want a declined or unsuccessful escape attempt recorded honestly, so that unfavorable outcomes remain valid play.
22. As Joel, I want the experiment to preserve remaining actions and unfinished turns at its endpoint, so that stopping does not invent game effects.
23. As Joel, I want autosave at committed decisions and manual save at pending choices, so that I can interrupt meaningful play.
24. As Joel, I want a fresh launch to restore the exact choice, state and randomness, so that resuming does not reroll or repeat effects.
25. As Joel, I want a failed save to leave live play unchanged, so that retrying cannot duplicate costs or consequences.
26. As Joel, I want undo only before new hidden information, so that I can correct decisions without rewriting revealed outcomes.
27. As Joel, I want stored replay moments with Next, Previous and camera control, so that I can narrate the attempt without new randomness.
28. As Joel, I want replay navigation to preserve the live session and original recording, so that inspecting the past cannot change the match.
29. As Joel, I want readable substitutes when art is absent, so that missing artwork does not prevent play.
30. As Joel, I want earlier Tony/Jacqueline saves and recordings preserved and accessible, so that this experiment does not invalidate accepted work.
31. As Joel, I want prior attempts preserved when starting another, so that trying another approach does not destroy evidence or recordings.
32. As Joel, I want corrupt or incompatible records refused without modification, so that recovery remains possible.

## Implementation Decisions

### Prepared position

| Element | Selected value |
| --- | --- |
| Context | Original Gathering, Standard, three investigators; Act 1 Trapped and agenda 1, with no pending trigger or doom threshold. |
| Start | Start of the investigation phase, before choosing its first investigator; no pending action or test. |
| Map and clues | All three investigators in revealed Study, shroud two; six clues on Study, zero held by the party. Only Study is in play. |
| Investigators | Printed attributes, health and sanity; zero damage. Tony and Patrice zero horror; Jacqueline two starting horror from two Arcane Research permanents. |
| Resources/discards | Zero resources and empty discard piles for all three. |
| Threats/assets | No enemies or threat-area cards; Internal Injury is not in play. Tony has Bounty Contracts with six bounties and no target. No other relevant assets beyond Jacqueline's two permanents. |
| Turns/limits | Each investigator may take one turn with three ordinary actions. Tony's restricted extra action is available but has no eligible Fight/Engage target. Jacqueline's reaction is unused this round. |
| Chaos bag | Original Standard composition: +1; two 0; three −1; two −2; −3; −4; two skull; cultist; tablet; auto-fail; elder sign. No initial bless/curse tokens. |

| Investigator | Initial hand | Fixed hidden draw prefix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tony | On the Hunt `03263` ×1 | Guts `01089` ×2, then On the Hunt `03263` ×1 |
| Patrice | Promise of Power `07032` ×1 | Lucky! `01080` ×2, then Unexpected Courage `01093` ×1 |
| Jacqueline | Clairvoyance `60408` ×1 | Clairvoyance `60408` ×1, then Eyes of the Dreamer `11067` ×2 |

Preserve the pinned starting-list quantities in the remaining hidden inventory. Do not replace unknown cards with playable inert cards. Unresolved basic-weakness slots remain outside reachable behavior and do not constitute completed campaign preparation. This arranged position does not prove that preceding legal campaign play reaches it. Fixed hidden deck order is fixture input, not player knowledge. Ordinary chaos draws are random and unbiased across physical tokens; privileged deterministic draws belong only to verification fixtures.

### Choices and stopping boundary

Offer Investigate, Draw, Resource, eligible commitments, optional abilities and voluntary End turn under the actual rules. One investigator finishes their turn before the next is selected. Preserve same-location eligibility and the ordinary one-card limit for each supporting investigator; the testing investigator may commit appropriate cards under the normal rules. Refuse invalid targets, unaffordable costs, inappropriate commitments and stale revisions without mutation.

Jacqueline may react to any investigator's eligible test at her location. Declining an initial reveal does not consume her reaction or suppress a later eligible curse-reveal opportunity. Preserve the round limit, all legal cancellation choices, additional draws, held-token custody and token cleanup. Resolve the testing investigator's own elder-sign effect. Support Lucky!'s original fast timing, cost and +2 effect without automatically selecting it.

Ordinary play stops at the **first fully settled action/test leaving six clues held by the group**. Complete commitments, token cleanup, mandatory consequences and legal after-test choices before presenting the closing decision:

- **Advance Act 1:** perform the group clue-spending decision, spend six, execute the full reverse, and expose Act 2. Put Hallway, Cellar, Attic and Parlor into play; discard every enemy in Study (none in this position); place all investigators in Hallway, revealing it; remove Study. Stop before further actions.
- **Finish the attempt without advancing:** preserve the resulting position and record the declined advancement. Do not invent a defeat or scenario resolution.

If all investigator turns finish before six clues are gathered, stop at the investigation-phase boundary before the enemy phase. Saving/closing may interrupt any pending decision without advancing it.

Ending this task does not end an unfinished investigator turn: preserve remaining actions, limits and game state. Keep the post-action player window even when the sixth clue comes from the third action. The endpoint is an explicit experiment boundary, not a rule forbidding further action after six clues. There is no continuation beyond this endpoint or migration promise into a future campaign implementation.

### Reachable-content closure

The following independent arguments define this prepared task. They must be challenged during verification; they are not permission to filter out legal choices:

1. Only ordinary successful Investigate tests gain clues, one at a time. Before the sixth discovery, every pre-reveal test window has fewer than six held clues. That test then settles and ordinary play stops before another begins. Thus no supported test loses its target to mid-test act advancement. General advancement during tests remains legal outside this selected task.
2. No enemies means no Fight/Evade/Engage target, opportunity attack, friendly fire or Gathering tablet damage. Study has no available movement destination before advancement. No Injury means no Injury action or turn-end damage.
3. Tony can draw at most three cards. Guts has no matching intellect icons and no willpower test occurs. On the Hunt can be committed to Investigate; its encounter-draw event timing does not occur.
4. Jacqueline draws at most three cards: either three ordinary Draw actions, or at most two plus one canceled-elder-sign draw during her own test. Helping another investigator uses that investigator's elder-sign effect. Her selected non-Fast assets cost at least three; gaining those resources from zero and playing an asset needs at least four actions. Their intellect icons remain usable.
5. Patrice cannot draw Lucky!, gain its one-resource cost and use it during a test before her third action. Unexpected Courage is reached only by a third Draw action. Before a non-final own test, at most her initial Promise can be in her discard, so her elder sign cannot shuffle a nonempty subset while leaving one card. On a final test, an eligible actual shuffle remains available, including selecting the retained card and persisting randomness. No later own Draw remains, and the selected partners' cards cannot draw for her. Later supporting commitments may change her discard without causing another test for her.
6. Only one Promise is reachable. Its commitment introduces one curse. Support real additional reveals, cancellation and token destinations. Ten-curse overflow and additional replacement assets are unreachable.
7. The Standard bag contains one physical cultist, held until test completion even if Jacqueline leaves two resolving tokens. At most one cultist horror per test and three own tests gives Tony at most three horror, Patrice three, and Jacqueline five including her starting horror. No damage is reachable. Defeat is therefore unreachable; no immunity is introduced.

New draw/resource gifts, extra actions/tests, enemies, pre-test clue gains or later phases invalidate these bounds and require scope review.

### Rules, continuity and presentation

- Use one local party session and its own supported record scope. Reuse existing production helpers and shared interactions when their contracts agree. The existing experiment states and token resolvers are deliberately narrow; changing an actor identifier does not establish correct party behavior. No general engine or interpreter is selected.
- Preserve the production **player observation → revision-bound choice → save candidate → install** authority boundary for both native UI and player driver. Observations and histories do not reveal future deck order or random state. The first risk-bearing check must exercise a real multi-investigator commitment/reaction and its continuation through this same boundary, against the independent expectations below.
- Autosave committed decisions and permit manual save at pending choices. Save the candidate before installing or displaying consequences. Persistence failure leaves live state, pending choices and future randomness unchanged; retries must not duplicate costs, tokens, clues, shuffles or map effects.
- Fresh-process reopen restores the exact state, held tokens, commitment/cancellation/fast-effect/after-test/closing choice, limits and randomness. Interrupted presentation has no rules authority. Records identify their required input, rules and application versions.
- Keep undo barriers at committed hidden revelations, including card draws and token reveals, not animation completion. An unobserved Patrice shuffle alone reveals no hidden information; undo can restore its prior state and randomness if it crosses no intervening revelation, but cannot cross the preceding test's token reveal. Retain intelligible undo history and preserve exported recordings.
- Replay consumes stored events/observations without new randomness or applying current rules. Next/Previous navigate meaningful moments with automatic camera direction and manual override. Returning to live play preserves the live session. Replay cannot overwrite a live save or rewrite the match.
- Preserve earlier experiment saves and recordings through retained compatible modes or an explicit tested compatible path. Refuse corrupt/incompatible records visibly with original bytes intact. Starting another attempt preserves previous records. No automatic migration is promised.
- Preserve the scenario area, investigator areas, test area, actor-versus-camera distinction, shared contextual controls, inspection, commitment markers, reveal shortcut, reduced-motion behavior and manual camera control. Explain costs, arithmetic, timing and consequences in readable game language. Show the actual map transition and honest completion state; do not expose fixture machinery as player controls.
- Prepare and verify selected new artwork before relying on it. Preserve the source archive and prior prepared collections. Runtime uses only the selected prepared asset collection, remains usable with readable substitutes, and works offline. Personal configuration, saves and recordings remain separate from portable artwork. No third-party payloads enter Git.
- All project-owned executable logic, tools and tests follow the accepted Rust implementation-language contract. Internal naming, decomposition, algorithms and reversible adapters remain delegated engineering judgment.

## Testing Decisions

Use the **existing highest behavioral seam: player observations and submitted revision-bound choices through the same rules authority as the native UI**. Joel accepted this seam with the coherent scope; no further interview is needed. Test available choices and observable consequences, not private types or implementation output used as its own oracle.

Prior art is the existing Jacqueline decision tests, Tony decision/continuity tests, actual driver-process reopening tests, and production tabletop registration checks. Cover the new party rules, persistence/replay integration and affected native controls through these established boundaries. Source-derived expectations remain independent of both old resolvers and any secondary implementation.

| Case | Independent expected result |
| --- | --- |
| Turn order and early End | Each investigator takes at most one turn; unused actions do not transfer. Camera focus never selects the actor. End cannot skip a pending test or consequence. |
| Shared commitment | A same-location supporting investigator contributes at most one appropriate card; Patrice's Promise adds four wild icons and one curse, then is discarded at test completion. Preserve legal decline and reject excess/invalid commitments. |
| Tony arithmetic | Intellect 3 with −2 fails Study shroud 2; one On the Hunt intellect icon changes the result to success. |
| Lucky tradeoff | Patrice Draw + Resource + Investigate can pay one for Lucky on eligible failure. Intellect 2 with −1 gives 1; Lucky gives 3 against difficulty 2. Lucky has no commitment icons. Decline remains legal. |
| Cultist and Lucky | Original Standard cultist is −1. Patrice's 2 − 1 fails at 1; Lucky brings it to 3, succeeding and preventing the failure-only horror. |
| Combined cancellation/curse | Jacqueline with Clairvoyance's intellect icon and Patrice's Promise has intellect 8. Reveal auto-fail, curse, 0; cancel auto-fail, then reveal −2: resolve total −4 and succeed at 4 against 2. Cancel curse and 0 instead: auto-fail remains, no clue is discovered. |
| Standard symbols and order | Skull is −X for Ghouls at the location, hence 0 here; cultist is −1 and causes 1 horror only on failure; tablet is −2 with damage only if a Ghoul is present, hence none here. Exercise every face, additional curse draws, legal multi-token resolution order and cleanup. |
| Investigator elder signs | Apply Tony's original Contracts effect, Patrice's original after-test shuffle option, or Jacqueline's own canceled-elder draw according to who tests. Jacqueline reacting on Tony/Patrice does not grant her own elder effect. |
| Patrice final shuffle | After a final test with an eligible discard, choose the card retained and actually shuffle the rest into her deck. Persist exact continuation; no fourth ordinary action or later draw is offered. |
| Prefix/asset closure | Support all three possible prefix draws and matching commitments. Refuse asset play due to actual action/resource insufficiency. No hidden tail card is revealed on any supported path. |
| Sixth clue on third action | Fully settle the test and after-test choices, then retain the final player window and closing spend/decline choice without artificial turn ending. |
| Advance/decline | Spend exactly six and complete the map transition, or retain Study and held clues. Neither branch silently continues to another turn/phase or invents campaign results. |
| No escape | If all turns end below six clues, finish without victory, defeat, enemy phase or scenario resolution. Preserve poor choices and unfavorable draws. |
| Undo | Permit only reversals that do not cross committed hidden information; preserve limits, previous state/randomness and recorded history, including after reopen. |
| Failed-save retry | Inject failure before installation, retry, and match an uninterrupted control: no duplicate effect, changed next draw or partially installed transition. |
| Fresh-process resume | Interrupt and reopen at commitment, cancellation, Lucky, final-shuffle and final-spend choices. Match pending choices, committed outcomes and unrevealed continuation against uninterrupted play. |
| Recorded replay | Navigate actual stored moments forward/back, then return to unchanged live state. No new randomness, recalculated outcome or save from the past. |
| Legacy/refusal | Earlier experiment records reopen through their supported paths; corrupt/unsupported records are preserved with a clear refusal. New attempts preserve prior records. |

Run the repository's required Rust/hygiene checks and proportionate affected native-path checks using isolated saves/settings and the existing verified tools. Exercise real artwork and readable substitutes. Existing test counts, screenshots or synthetic input do not establish rules fidelity or owner experience beyond the behavior actually exercised.

Owner acceptance uses **at most two sessions of 20 minutes each, including retries**:

- Session 1 exercises cooperation, interruption/resume and an escape attempt.
- Session 2 changes investigator order/ability allocation, includes decline or unsuccessful completion as needed, and narrates stored replay.

Prepare technical evidence before consuming owner attention. Outcome luck does not mandate another run. Joel judges clarity, pacing, control burden and whether this task is worth playing; automation cannot supply that verdict. These checks do not establish recurrent-use fitness or the complete lifecycle of any investigator.

## Out of Scope

Full scenario setup or complete The Gathering; enemy/upkeep/mythos phases; play after the declared endpoint; movement/actions in newly revealed locations after advancement; combat or defeat machinery unsupported by this position; full-deck shuffling/drawing beyond the bounded Patrice continuation; actual random-basic-weakness preparation; upgrades and successor decks; arbitrary content support; runtime LLM adjudication; general engine/DSL/framework; automatic record migration; unrelated refactors or new diagnostic tools; video encoding/upload/publication; paid services; redistribution of source assets.

The original Night of the Zealot campaign remains the complete-delivery goal and remains unmet. Acceptance of this attempt cannot be used as proof of a complete scenario, campaign, reusable engine or normal randomly prepared deck play.

## Further Notes

### Authority, classification, appetite and stopping

- Owner and acceptance authority: Joel (`joeloverbeck`). Baseline: `7083162607cc910632d1aaedbc2a82581fe54282`.
- The incumbent is the accepted isolated test and Tony-turn paths; they remain available. This work uses the smallest local party implementation needed for the selected real-card task, rather than building general infrastructure first.
- This is a **decision-only gameplay experiment** for judging connected party cooperation and first-act progression through the real player, persistence and presentation paths. Its defining result is Joel completing or intentionally terminating this exact task and judging its clarity/burden. It does not confer product-like authority on a broader engine or establish campaign readiness. Later promotion/reuse beyond this scope requires the applicable evidence and acceptance.
- This one issue owns the selected increment. It displaces full-scenario implementation until this bounded party path is inspected. No separate maintenance, architecture or tooling lane is activated. The existing closed #1, #2 and #22 are accepted evidence, not open blockers.
- **32 aggregate active engineering hours**, counting delegated work, source preflight, implementation, asset preparation, tests, native verification and reviews. **Two owner sessions, each at most 20 minutes**, counting retries. No paid services. These are prospective ceilings, unconsumed by implementation at publication, not delivery promises. Earlier allowances do not reset or transfer here.
- First exercise the multi-investigator commitment/reaction and save/reopen path against the worked cases before expanding presentation. Keep the default early stops: two active hours without an inspectable acceptance-bearing increment; three failed repair cycles at the same boundary; three review passes expanding an open semantic family; approximately doubled expected surface; an unapproved capability/pipeline; or any effort/human-burden limit. Investigate findings and distinguish implementation defects from invalid expectations before repair.
- Stop on unverifiable governing inputs, a material unresolved source interpretation, or failed reachable-content closure before implementing around it. Report the exact evidence and recommend the smallest correction or reduced promise. No silent unsupported behavior, automatic extension or fresh adjacent lane follows. At the limit, preserve the candidate and return for adopt/reject/narrow/park/reframe or explicitly authorized continuation. Unadopted or failed experimental behavior must not gain authoritative dependents/default-path publication through inertia.
- `ready-for-agent` records bounded readiness. This publication does **not** activate implementation, unattended continuation, native sessions, commit/push, PR, merge or owner acceptance. Future implementation activation and exact production publication retain their separate authority. Recheck baseline, issue state and source identities before execution. Record effort, review cycles and remaining owner allowance here during authorized execution; unattended work additionally requires the repository's durable-state requirements.
- The source set, precedence, finite obligation bounds, independent expectations and input identities below support constructing this bounded candidate. They do not assert that it has run. A local prototype or secondary implementation must not substitute for the intended Rust/native consumer's checks.

### Source set, precedence and custody

Use the accepted Chapter One/original English baseline: applicable errata and the pinned taboo overlay; specific card/scenario exceptions over general rules; absolute prohibitions and applicable encounter-over-player precedence; Rules Reference over Learn to Play; expansion rules for bless/curse. ArkhamDB is metadata/transport evidence and the Haskell reference is secondary evidence, neither an independent rules authority. The Grim Rule does not license permanent invented engine rulings. A new campaign/latest-taboo refresh is not part of this prepared attempt.

The immutable [source reconciliation](https://github.com/joeloverbeck/arkham-unfolded/blob/7083162607cc910632d1aaedbc2a82581fe54282/docs/research/issue-1-source-reconciliation.md), [evidence manifest](https://github.com/joeloverbeck/arkham-unfolded/blob/7083162607cc910632d1aaedbc2a82581fe54282/docs/research/issue-1-evidence.json) and [starting-deck projection](https://github.com/joeloverbeck/arkham-unfolded/blob/7083162607cc910632d1aaedbc2a82581fe54282/docs/research/issue-1-decks.json) bind the exact supplied inputs. Starting deck identities are Tony `5392133` v0.5, Patrice `5391062` v0.7 and Jacqueline `5389418` v0.9. Their historical descriptions/trauma and successors are not current campaign state. Existing relevant face bindings and precedent are in the immutable [Tony preparation](https://github.com/joeloverbeck/arkham-unfolded/blob/7083162607cc910632d1aaedbc2a82581fe54282/docs/research/tony-turn-preparation.md).

| [Original Night of the Zealot guide](https://cdn.svc.asmodee.net/production-fantasyflightgames/uploads/2026/09/night_of_the_zealot_campaign_guide.pdf) | SHA-256 `132bb78a2c70245d2aa8037bab39784f42431b01c02ffa9d5b44d2edc10e13fb`; original campaign and Standard bag context. |
| [Legacy FAQ 2.5](https://images-cdn.fantasyflightgames.com/filer_public/c1/d0/c1d0fab6-7fa6-4ce2-af6a-16416381a19b/ahc_faq_v25_february_2026-web.pdf) | SHA-256 `35c82dc070332acd7863eb6d464641ea79e4657b68ff4f1873538e0bcac6b2e7`; original/errata precedence, choices, multiple tokens and automatic outcomes. |

All nine retained PDF/API inputs matched the evidence manifest during preparation on 2026-10-31. They remain retrievable machine-local copies; this is not an independent backup guarantee. Preserve required exact bytes in declared durable owner-controlled custody before dependent long-term fidelity/replay claims. Missing or changed bytes must be reported, not silently replaced. This is bounded source preflight, not a new evidence-management product.

Original English card images were visually inspected and hashed. Archive classification supplies provenance, not publisher authentication. The following additionally checked faces bind the new obligations:

| Card side | Code / variant | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |

Act 1 has no Objective timing restriction; Act 2 owns the end-of-round restriction. Hallway's revealed side has no further triggered effect. General mid-test act advancement removing a test target remains outside the selected endpoint; no unverified abort interpretation is adopted. The Standard reference was rechecked during synthesis and corrected a preparation arithmetic typo: cultist is −1, not −2. This changes no selected feature or expected Lucky! success outcome.

Keep the accepted [prepared-runtime-assets decision](https://github.com/joeloverbeck/arkham-unfolded/blob/7083162607cc910632d1aaedbc2a82581fe54282/docs/adr/0001-prepared-runtime-assets.md) and [persistent-table-areas decision](https://github.com/joeloverbeck/arkham-unfolded/blob/7083162607cc910632d1aaedbc2a82581fe54282/docs/adr/0002-persistent-table-areas.md). No new ADR or glossary term is required merely to select this task.

This issue is self-contained for its accepted contract and links immutable supporting evidence; it does not rely on the uncommitted preparation document being available on GitHub. Consulted constitution revision 2026-09-30.1: full text during preparation; AUTH-1–3, WORK-1–6, AGENT-5, OPS-1–7 and PUB-1 rechecked for this readiness/publication transition. Also applicable from preparation: PURP-2–5, EVID-2–8, SEM-1/2, REP-1/2, AGENT-3 and GOV-1–3.

comments.text:
Implementation activated by Joel's explicit `$implement "Please implement GitHub #55."` invocation on 2026-10-31. Fixed point: `7083162607cc910632d1aaedbc2a82581fe54282`, current branch `main`. Existing untracked `docs/research/next-playable-segment-preparation.md` is outside the implementation and will be preserved.

The selected result remains the decision-only prepared Study escape attempt specified here. First increment: source preflight, then the real party commitment/Jacqueline-reaction continuation through revision-bound player choices and save-before-install/reopen, using this issue's independent worked expectations. The intermittent startup lag has a measured application-level cause and a verified local workaround.

The renderer sometimes placed upload staging in CPU-visible GPU BAR memory. The allocation reported success, but copying roughly 300 KB took about 22 milliseconds. Requiring system-memory staging reduced comparable writes to approximately 0.03 milliseconds and restored rendering from roughly 11 to 60 updates per second. Restoring the original allocation policy reproduced the slowdown.

The local repair narrows this change to internal transient upload buffers on the observed Linux/Vulkan NVIDIA RTX 2080 Ti. It preserves the pinned renderer dependency's licenses and provenance, leaves unrelated adapters and buffers on their existing path, and retains the rendering-health guard. It applies automatically through the ordinary launch command.

Verification passed: 297 application tests, 50 tool tests, 7 allocation-policy tests, Clippy, formatting, tracked-file hygiene, and independent Standards/Spec reviews. Four full-art party launches through ordinary Cargo were healthy, including the owner's exact command and original save path. The original save remained byte-identical. Camera movement was exercised with synthetic input while rendering remained healthy; Tony and Jacqueline also passed bounded startup smoke checks.

This is a local application workaround, not a repaired NVIDIA driver or a guarantee against all future graphics failures. Physical-input and owner gameplay acceptance remain separate. Code has not been pushed, merged or published, and this update does not close #55.
